newsitem.title: USA: NYSE to decide within six months on move - Grasso.
newsitem.headline: NYSE to decide within six months on move - Grasso.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange will decide within the next six months whether to move from its current location at the corner of Broad and Wall streets to a different site in New York, NYSE Chairman Richard Grasso said Friday.

"We are for the first time looking at alternative sites. They will be in the city of New York, preferably in lower Manhattan," Grasso said at a Financial Executives Institute luncheon in Boston. "In the next six months, we will make a decision."
The NYSE has invested $1 billion during the past 10 years in technology to update its communications systems, but much of that investment would have to be scrapped if the exchange moved, he said.
s become a pressing issue for the exchange at a time when Grasso has made a priority of listing more non-U.S. companies.
In the United States, the NYSE lists 2,600 of the 3,300 companies that meet its standards, but only 280 of the 2,800 companies around the world that are eligible, he said.

Adding the remaining 700 U.S. companies would add $640 billion in market valuation to the NYSE, whereas adding the 800 largest non-U.S. companies would double the exchange's market value of $6.6 trillion.
In November, Deutsche Telekom, slated for privatization, is set to list on the NYSE, adding its market capitalization of $115 billion.
"When you start to tumble numbers, it is a very, very early point in the dawning of globalization of equity markets," Grasso said.
